stem: Solve ${=ineq}$ for $x$, where $x$ is a real number. Then mark the solution on the number line: choose where the solution starts and where it ends, and make each end hollow if that number is not included, or filled if it is.
solution: Whatever you do to one part of a double inequality you must do to all three parts, so that both inequalities stay true together.
Read it from the smaller number up: ${=s3}$. So the solution starts at ${=from_v}$ and ends at ${=to}$.
notes: Every instance has a negative coefficient AND one $<$ with one $\le$, by design. Dividing by the negative number gives the right two endpoints either way, so the reversal error can only show as wrong circles: a student who leaves the signs in their original order writes the numbers in ascending order but keeps the left sign on the left and the right sign on the right, giving the opposite circles with the right endpoints. Signature of negative-no-reverse per row (right endpoints, circles swapped): [-1, 3), [-2, 1), (-2, 5], (-1, 2]. A both-open or both-closed instance would hide the error entirely and is excluded. LIMIT: the line grades the finished interval, not the working, so a student who divides without reversing but then keeps each circle with its own number draws the correct picture and passes undetected; only the circle-swapped version is visible. endpoint-inclusion-wrong can also be an ordinary hollow/filled slip; it is mapped to negative-no-reverse because the mixed-sign, negative-coefficient design makes that the dominant cause. Signature of operate-on-middle-only (constant removed from the middle only, then every part divided): (-3, 1], (-3, 0], [-4, 3), [-3, 0). interval-wrong is also fired by sign slips in the quotient (for example a mirrored interval) and by arithmetic slips; those are named here and not separately mapped, since no misconception on this objective describes them.
